title: Punishment for SAF Officers Involved in Exercises that Lead to Deaths or Injuries
what_it_is: Punishment for SAF Officers Involved in Exercises that Lead to Deaths or Injuries

sections.label: Punishments for two SAF officers
sections.summary: A question asked the Minister for Defence what punishments the two SAF officers received for their roles in a 2012 training exercise in which a National Serviceman died.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Defence what are the punishments that have been given to the two SAF officers for their roles during a training exercise in 2012 in which a National Serviceman died as a result of an allergic reaction to smoke grenades after their conviction under military law.

sections.label: Coroner findings and AGC decision
sections.summary: The Coroner found PTE Lee died from an acute allergic reaction to zinc chloride fumes, and the AGC decided not to prosecute as the reaction was unforeseen and unlikely to have been predicted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The Coroner concluded that PTE Lee's death was due to "an acute allergic reaction to zinc chloride due to inhalation of zinc chloride fumes." It "could not be definitive whether in the deceased's case the reaction was due to the inhalation of excessive fumes or the mere inhalation of fumes" at paragraph 77 of the Coroner's findings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Because of these findings and conclusions, AGC decided not to prosecute anyone as the cause of death was an unforeseen allergic reaction that was unlikely to have been predicted.

sections.label: SAF officers charged under military law
sections.summary: After the AGC's decision not to prosecute, the two SAF officers were charged under military law in November 2013 for breaching safety regulations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Following the AGC's decision not to prosecute, the two SAF officers were charged under military law in November 2013 for breaching safety regulations.

sections.label: Cost of promotion delays
sections.summary: The monetary cost of the promotion delays is significant, amounting to about half of their total annual salaries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The monetary cost of the promotion delays is significant, amounting to about half of their total annual salaries.

sections.label: Punishment and Coroner's findings
sections.summary: The level of punishment has to take into account the Coroner's findings that PTE Lee's fatal allergic reaction was unlikely to have been predicted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The level of punishment has to take into account the Coroner's findings that PTE Lee's fatal allergic reaction was unlikely to have been predicted.

sections.label: Zinc chloride allergy testing and SAF switch
sections.summary: There is no reliable test recommended by health experts to diagnose allergy to zinc chloride, and after a safety review SAF switched to alternatives that do not release zinc chloride fumes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, there is no reliable test recommended by health experts to diagnose allergy to zinc chloride.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: After the safety review following this case, SAF switched to alternatives which do not release zinc chloride fumes.

sections.label: Coroner's Inquiry and AGC decision
sections.summary: The Coroner's Inquiry found the allergic reaction unlikely to have been predicted and not reckless or negligent, so AGC decided against criminal prosecution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: But regardless of their intent, over the course of an open inquiry where the family was present, all the findings presented, the Coroner's Inquiry (CI) did not find that their actions were reckless and negligent, but that the allergic reaction was "unlikely to have been predicted".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Therefore, AGC decided that the officers would not be prosecuted in criminal Courts.

sections.label: MINDEF law and moral hazard
sections.summary: The Member asks whether MINDEF will amend the law to reduce moral hazard of officers not abiding by training safety regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would MINDEF amend this law at least to reduce the possible moral hazard of any officers not taking sufficient care and caution in abiding by established TSRs during training exercises?

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I do not have the full slate of details, but the general rule is the punishment must match the offence.

sections.label: Moral hazard and SAF servicemen
sections.summary: The response states there is less moral hazard because SAF servicemen know rash and negligent acts are not protected and AGC can prosecute.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Central to the question is what the Member talked about – moral hazard.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: There is less of a moral hazard because the SAF Servicemen know that if they act in a rash and negligent way, they are not protected.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The AGC can prosecute them in the criminal Courts.

sections.label: Tragic case and processes complied
sections.summary: The passage states the case is tragic, unexpected and unintended, and that full processes were complied with.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: For this case, it is tragic, it is unexpected, it is unintended, full processes were complied with.
